title: Tourist Season
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: August. The town full of strangers. Wood frames their whale-watching photos and takes notes.

panels.composition: The frame shop, August. A TOURIST COUPLE in matching fleece with a photograph: a gray smudge on gray water.

characters.pose: in matching fleece, holding a photo

image.prompt: a couple in matching fleece vests holding out a photograph of a gray smudge on gray water at a frame-shop counter, a young man behind it

panels.composition: The photo. The smudge. Wood's face, professional.

balloons.text: We saw it from the highway. Just — there. It was so real.
The highway is where most of the real things are seen from.

image.prompt: close-up of a young man keeping a professional face while examining a photo of a gray smudge

panels.composition: Wood choosing a frame. Ornate. Gold. The most expensive one. The couple thrilled.

characters.pose: holding up an ornate gold frame

image.prompt: a young man holding up an ornate gold frame to a delighted couple in matching fleece

panels.composition: After. The shop empty. Wood at the counter, drawing the couple from memory with great precision and no cruelty at all. He is surprised by that.
props: pad with a careful drawing of the couple

image.prompt: a young man alone at a frame-shop counter drawing a careful affectionate sketch of a couple in fleece vests and looking surprised at his own drawing, black and white

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Tourist Season, first instance. The cruelty he planned doesn't arrive. He notices.
